class.name: SimulationDomain
class.brief_description: An isolated container representing a physics space, scenario, and canvas.
class.description:
[admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i][/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition]
[admonition type="crucial"] [b]This type is strictly managed and must NEVER be created or destroyed by user code![/b] [SimulationDomain]s are extremely stringent about their operating conditions as they expect to be tied closely to a [manualcref=T:Star3D.World.Galaxy.WorldInstance] and, in the event that a [SimulationDomain] is destroyed or disconnected from a still-operating [manualcref=T:Star3D.World.Galaxy.WorldInstance], it will forcibly crash the game to prevent the inevitable data corruption that will result from you doing this.
You have been warned! [/admonition]
An isolated container representing both a 2D and 3D physics space, a render scenario, and a canvas. This is different than a [SubViewport] in that it cannot be rendered to a target; instead, it is intended to be representative of a loaded game world with its own isolated rendering and physics.

method.name: set_conservatory_callbacks
method.description: Sets the low level references to the game's code needed to crash the game, verify the destruction of [SimulationDomain]s, and check if the current program is the game client. [b]Note:[/b] As a modder, you should never call this. This is closely managed by the game and requires extremely specific conditions to use, otherwise the game will crash.

method.name: destroy
method.description: The equivalent of [code]Free[/code] for this instance. This [b]MUST[/b] be called; using [code]Free[/code] will crash the game. [b]Note:[/b] As a modder, you should never call this. This is closely managed by the game and requires extremely specific conditions to use, otherwise the game will crash.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], this instance is valid and can be used. Only [code]false[/code] if destroyed and a reference to it is kept, which should never happen.

If [code]true[/code], this instance is the current one being rendered to the game client's screen. This is always [code]true[/code] on the server no matter what, because on servers every [SimulationDomain] is always active.
The [RID] of the physics space used for 2D physics in this [SimulationDomain].
The [RID] of the physics space used for 3D physics in this [SimulationDomain].
The [RID] of the canvas used for 2D rendering in this [SimulationDomain]. Not likely to be used in [i]The Conservatory[/i], but here for completeness.
The [RID] of the scenario used for 3D rendering in this [SimulationDomain].
